name: F5 BIG-IP configuration
comment:
A BIG-IP `bigip.conf` / `.scf`. Not Tcl — but an `ltm rule` body *is* Tcl, and is included as such here, exactly as the server walks it with the iRules dialect. Before this grammar, every Tcl-family language was pointed at `tcl.tmLanguage.json`, which contains no BIG-IP rule at all, so a config was painted with Tcl rules and then replaced wholesale once semantic tokens arrived (issue #903).

The scopes are deliberately the *less specific* members of the families `package.json` maps the server's BIG-IP token types to: the server can tell a pool from a monitor from a profile and emits `entity.name.type.pool.bigip`; a static grammar usually cannot, so it emits `entity.name.type.bigip`. Both live under `entity.name.type`, so a theme colours them identically — the grammar is less precise than the server, and never contradicts it.

irule.comment: `ltm rule /Common/name { … }` — the body is an iRule, i.e. Tcl. The end pattern is a closing brace in column 0, which is where tmsh writes it; a brace nested in the script is indented and so cannot end the block early.

typed-object-reference.comment: A reference whose *type* is named by the preceding word — the one case where a static grammar can be as specific as the server, so it is. The name word itself is a `property` to the server (`pool`, `profiles`, `vlans` all come back as `property`), not a keyword: painting it `keyword.other` made it flip colour the moment semantic tokens arrived. The value class excludes braces: `vlans { /Common/internal }` opens a block, and `(\S+)` captured the `{` itself as the object name.

declaration.comment: A top-level object declaration — `<module> <type> ?<subtype>? /Partition/name {`. The module and type words are the config's structure.

encrypted.comment: An encrypted secret — tmsh writes these as `$M$…`. Scoped so a theme can visibly mark it, matching the server's `encrypted` type.
encrypted.name: string.other.encrypted.bigip

member-path.comment: A pool-member / virtual-destination path, `/Partition/<address>:<port>`. The name component *is* an address, and the server types it as one — so it must not fall through to #object-path and be painted as an object name instead, which is the one place these two grammars could have contradicted each other.

object-path.comment: An object path, `/Partition/name`, optionally with a route domain (`%1`) and a port (`:80`). The partition is a namespace and is scoped as one, exactly as the server does; the object itself gets the generic `entity.name.type.bigip` because a bare path does not say what kind of object it names.

ip-address.comment: IPv4 (with optional CIDR / route domain / port) and IPv6.

monitor-expression.comment: `monitor` takes an expression, not merely a reference: `default`, `none`, `M1 and M2`, or `min N of { M1 M2 }` (see rust/tcl-bigip/src/value/monitor_expression.rs). The plain `monitor <ref>` rule scoped the next word as the monitor object, which paints `min` — and `default`/`none` — as a monitor name. The server types the *whole* expression as `monitor`, keywords and the count included, so this does too: less specific than the server is fine, differently coloured is not.

patterns.comment: The expression's own words. The server types these `monitor` too.
patterns.name: entity.name.type.monitor.bigip

patterns.comment: The `N` of `min N of` — a count, but the server types it `monitor`, so a `number` scope here would contradict it.
patterns.name: entity.name.type.monitor.bigip

patterns.comment: Each monitor named in the expression.

property-name.comment:
A property whose value is a *block* — `vlans { … }`, `members { … }`, `records { … }`. The typed rules above cannot reach these because their value is `{`, not a reference.

The match must START at the word, not at the indentation. TextMate picks the pattern whose match begins **leftmost**, and only breaks ties by list order — so an `^\s+(word)` rule starts at column 0 and beats every rule on the line no matter where it is listed. Written that way, it silently disabled `monitor-expression` and the typed references entirely.
